title: orch push via send-keys lands in composer but does not submit; report loss is recurring
description: Worker and sidecar completion reports are pushed to the orchestrator pane as a one-line send-keys message (the CAM-55 push model, text plus Enter atomic in one call). Recurring failure observed by the operator (multiple times, latest 2026-07-06): the pushed line lands in the orchestrator TUI composer but the Enter does not submit, so the message sits unsent and the orchestrator never receives the report. Concrete instance: the ship-phase gates-failed report for CAM-118 (14:26 UTC) sat un-submitted in the composer; the orchestrator only learned of the failure when the operator mentioned it, then had to reconstruct the outcome from cam-worker-events.jsonl. Atomic text+Enter (CAM-55) is necessary but evidently not sufficient: the likely mechanism is a composer race when the TUI is busy (streaming, rendering, or mid-turn) when the keys arrive, with the trailing Enter consumed as a newline or dropped. Fix direction, in line with the structured-handback decision (CAM-75/77/78: pane push is only a wake-up, durable truth lives in files): (a) delivery verification in the single pusher (sidecar): after send-keys, verify submission (e.g. capture-pane shows the line left the composer, or pane state check) and retry with bounded backoff; (b) treat unverifiable delivery as a wedge signal: emit an event (push-undelivered) so the flight recorder shows it; (c) since the durable truth already exists (worker-report.json, cam-worker-events.jsonl, ship-phase-result events), the orchestrator side needs only the wake-up to be reliable, no content needs to travel in the pane line. Do NOT parse pane scrollback as the fix (rendered markdown is lossy, the known capture-pane trap). Cross-refs: CAM-195 (evented terminals the orch can derive on wake), CAM-55 (atomic send-keys decision), CAM-167 (worker pane lifecycle).
